key_insight: QuTOP uses offline oracle knowledge to select quantum hardware and compiler settings jointly, avoiding the limitations of choosing a device before tuning compilation.
engineering_relevance: Rule-guided prediction offers a way to improve circuit execution fidelity while reducing configuration-selection latency without iterative online search.
method: Build QuOPTBench by exhaustively searching configurations for 268 quantum circuits.
Use an LLM to extract transferable configuration-selection rules from sampled circuits.
Combine these rules with predictors trained on enumerated configuration data to select configurations for new circuits.
evidence_signal: The study evaluates ten representative LLMs, finds vanilla models far from oracle performance, and reports that QuTOP achieves the strongest overall quality–latency balance among evaluated baselines.
watch_item: Offline enumeration adds upfront cost, and changing hardware characteristics may require refreshing the learned rules and predictors.
paper_title: Turning Quantum Compiler Configuration Selection Upside Down: A Top-Down Paradigm
